title: Later Qin
capsule: The Later Qin (後秦, 384–417) was a Qiang-led state founded by Yao Chang in the Guanzhong basin around Chang'an during the Sixteen Kingdoms period, after he rebelled against Former Qin following the Battle of Fei River (383). Under Yao Xing (r. 394–416) the state reached its widest extent, patronizing Buddhist institutions and sponsoring the Central Asian monk Kumārajīva — who produced between 401 and 413 the definitive Chinese translations of the Lotus Sutra, the Diamond Sutra, and other canonical texts. Eastern Jin forces under Liu Yu invaded in 416–17, capturing Chang'an and executing the last ruler Yao Hong, extinguishing the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Later Qin core territory in Guanzhong is well documented in Chinese annals; the exact northern and western limits of its transient control are imprecisely defined.
